questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The academic programme, because of Norway's EEA position. Also because UiB has a good law of the course as well as a multidisciplinary approach.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a very good experience with my academic development during my Erasmus.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: very easy, I got a lot of info on my mail as well as two introductions days only for exchange students.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: info about everything in the introduction week, as well as email and contact info for the administration if we wanted more assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: No additional comments

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: They have a union called Sammen that offer all exchange students housing.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I had a full equipped and functional kitchen shared with one other Erasmus student.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That it might be a bit tiny and you're living in shared rooms, but its the best - and cheappest - way to live during the Erasmus stay, because you live with all the other exchange students.

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: No additional comments

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is a course catalogue on their website - which UiB also send to you on your email. I has all the info that you need to find the courses you find interesting and its also easy to register as you just click on the courses you like.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You select from their course catalogue, which UiB sends you a link to. So very easy, it's just clicking on the course you want.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Info on webpage and you could ask their office

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful, got all my first priorities

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Maybe register for one or two extra courses, because then you can try to attend a few different courses and afterwards cancel the course you find least interesting. (you have 3 weeks after the semester start before you have to "lock in" the course you want)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was very satisfied with the academic programme, the courses, the lectures, the teaches and everything.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Same as UCPH, but easy to pass the exam. I probably spend 30 hours per week on classes and self-studying.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More interdisciplinary. And also the fact that it was only the head of the course who was the teacher.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Law of the Sea, Comparative Private Law, EU and EEA law and policymaking

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Law of the sea, because of the lector Ignacio. He just had a way of inspiring through his lectures.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I didnt encounter any unexpected costs

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I didn't buy any book's since a lot of the study-material was articles of excerpts that was for free online. Other than that I just used the uni library to do my readings. Local transport was very cheap compared to Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was very satisfied. They had a lot of non-academic opportunities - clubs, sports, social events, study help etc

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: all sorts of activities - too many to start listing.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: just go for whatever you find interesting. I liked the hiking, football and swimming. But there I a lot to do.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hiking in the nature. That's definitely the main one. Other than that there is a lot of interesting museums and art galleries.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: very easy, similar to Copenhagen.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just cross your own boundaries, even though it might be frightening. Try and small-talk in danish/norwegian in every possible place. Specially the mentors in the introduction week. Then you have some to talk to when the semester starts. After that it gets more easy.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none, maybe the language, but it got better very fast

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The outdoor, hiking, life-style

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: stay at sammen housing, spend time in the nature and talk with the locals and international exchange student

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think that the current information is more than satisfactory.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: personal-, social-, linguistic- and academic development

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being on you're own in a new place

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I don't have any additional comments

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
